title: How many independent points the radiation behaves like
spoken: The effective count equals the energy divided by k B times B times the frequency.
explanation: Matching the radiation's entropy change to a gas of independent points gives the number of points the gas would need. It is read off a comparison, not counted.
assumptions: Dilute radiation: the density is low enough, relative to temperature, that Wien's law describes the spectrum.
These are modern teaching equations in SI notation, with A and B for the paper's alpha and beta; they are not a transcription of the printed paper.
The gas comparison assumes n independent points whose chance of all lying in a fraction f of the volume is f to the n.

notes.title: Effective count
notes.explanation: The number of independent points a gas would need to show the same logarithmic entropy change. Nothing here observes points.

notes.title: Energy in the band
notes.explanation: The radiation's energy within the narrow band, held fixed while the volume changes.

notes.title: Boltzmann's constant
notes.explanation: The gas side of the comparison: n points change entropy by n k_B ln f.

notes.title: Spectral constant B
notes.explanation: From the Wien spectrum; B times the frequency divided by the temperature is a pure number.

notes.title: Frequency of the band
notes.explanation: The band's frequency. The count falls as the frequency rises for the same energy.

notes.title: Two coefficients set equal
notes.explanation: Both entropy changes are a coefficient times ln f. Setting the coefficients equal is the comparison; it is a correspondence, not a derivation that light is made of points.
